title: Electrical power and energy
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:36Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point covers energy as power times time and billing in kWh, but it does not teach P = VI, which the new point requires, so adapting it would need a new step and it is a different scope from the new point.

draft.title: Electrical power and energy
card: Electrical power is the rate at which a device transfers energy. P = VI, where P is in watts (W), V is in volts (V) and I is in amperes (A).
Energy transferred = power × time, or E = Pt. With P in watts and t in seconds, E is in joules (J). One watt is one joule per second.
Electricity bills use the kilowatt-hour (kWh). It is the energy used by a 1 kW device running for 1 hour.
To find kWh, change power to kilowatts and time to hours, then multiply. 1 kWh = 3.6 million joules.
draft.remember: Power is VI. Energy is power × time, and a kWh is 1 kW for 1 hour.

a.q: A heater runs from a 240 V supply and draws a current of 5.0 A. What is its power?
a.why: P = VI = 240 × 5.0 = 1200 W. Dividing V by I gives 48, which is a resistance in ohms, not a power.
a.clue: Multiply the voltage by the current.

b.q: Priya runs a 2000 W fan heater for 3 hours. How much energy does she use, as billed?
b.why: Change 2000 W to 2 kW, then E = 2 × 3 = 6 kWh. Leaving the power in watts gives 6000, which is in watt-hours, not kilowatt-hours.
b.clue: Change watts to kilowatts before multiplying by hours.
